en: Taal Volcano features a lake inside its main crater that contains Volcano Island, making it an island within a lake on an island.
Mount Pulag's famous sea of clouds occurs because its 2,928-meter peak rises above the condensation level of moist air from Benguet.
Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Lake Sebu in South Cotabato is one of the few Philippine lakes that never dries up, sustained year-round by natural springs.
Palawan is the longest Philippine province, stretching 425 kilometers, and acts as a biological corridor connecting Asia to Borneo rainforests.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea contains over 600 fish species and 360 coral species, making it a marine biodiversity hotspot.
Baguio City earns the title Summer Capital because its 1,500-meter elevation keeps its average annual temperature at a cool 18 degrees Celsius.
Bohol's Chocolate Hills consist of exactly 1,268 symmetrical cone-shaped karst limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
Rafflesia schadenbergiana, found only in Mount Apo, produces the largest individual flower in the Philippines, measuring up to one meter across.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for having the most perfect cone shape among all active volcanoes worldwide.
The Verde Island Passage between Batangas and Mindoro is scientifically recognized as the center of marine shorefish biodiversity globally.
Pangasinan's Hundred Islands National Park actually contains exactly 124 islands during low tide, which are ancient uplifted coral reefs.
